title: Gluing O-linear maps on one covering family
statement: Let C be a site with the fiber products U_i\times_U U_j and V\times_U U_i used below [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], O a sheaf of commutative rings, and F,G sheaves of O-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Given an object U and a covering family {U_i\to U}, every family of O|_{U_i}-linear morphisms φ_i:F|_{U_i}\to G|_{U_i} that agrees after restriction to U_i\times_U U_j glues to a unique O|_U-linear morphism φ:F|_U\to G|_U.

proof.text: Work in the localized site C/U. For each object V/U, the site base-change axiom makes {V×_U U_i→V} a covering. For x∈F(V), the local maps give sections φ_i(x|_{V×_U U_i}) of G on these members. On (V×_U U_i)×_V(V×_U U_j)=V×_U(U_i×_U U_j) the two sections agree because the restrictions of φ_i and φ_j agree on U_i×_U U_j. The sheaf equalizer axiom for the underlying sheaf of abelian groups G therefore gives a unique section φ_V(x)∈G(V) restricting to all these sections. Applying the same uniqueness to sums and to restrictions shows additivity and naturality, so the φ_V form a morphism of sheaves of abelian groups F|_U→G|_U.

The glued morphism restricts to φ_i: on U_i the two maps have the same restrictions on the pulled-back covering family, so uniqueness in the sheaf axiom identifies them. If another morphism has the same restrictions, its value on every section x∈F(V) has the same restrictions on the covering V×_U U_i→V and hence equals φ_V(x); thus the glued morphism is unique.

The glued map is O|_U-linear. For a∈O(V) and x∈F(V), on every member V×_U U_i of the covering its value is φ_i(a x)=a|_{V×_U U_i} φ_i(x), since each φ_i is O|_{U_i}-linear and scalar multiplication restricts sectionwise. The sheaf uniqueness assertion then gives φ_V(a x)=a φ_V(x). Hence φ is a morphism of sheaves of O|_U-modules, as required.
